name: @tessa/console
description: Tessa Console — the terminal surface. ConPTY under xterm, one WebSocket in the main process.

scripts.typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.preload.json --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.web.json --noEmit

$comment: NO "type": "module" — deliberate, same as apps/orb. A sandboxed Electron preload CANNOT be an
ES module; declaring the package ESM makes electron-vite emit ESM for main AND preload, and the
preload then fails to load at runtime. Source is ESM TypeScript either way; electron-vite
transpiles main/preload to CJS and the renderer stays ESM via Vite.
DEPENDENCY CLASS IS THE EXTERNALIZATION SWITCH. electron-vite externalizes `dependencies` and
- @lydell/node-pty and ws are in `dependencies` — externalized, required at runtime. node-pty
resolves its binary via a runtime dynamic require plus an on-disk package.json read, so
bundling it is fatal. Bundling ws would drag in its optional native deps (bufferutil,
- @tessa/protocol and @tessa/tokens are devDependencies ON PURPOSE. @tessa/protocol's entry is raw
TypeScript (src/index.ts, importing ./enums.generated.ts). Externalized, that becomes a
runtime require() of a .ts file and main crashes on launch. As devDeps they are bundled.
- react/react-dom/@xterm/* are renderer-only; Vite bundles the renderer regardless of class.
vite is pinned to 7.3.6, NOT 8.x. electron-vite 5.0.0 peer-deps vite ^5||^6||^7; supporting vite 8
required a new MAJOR (electron-vite 6.0.0-beta.1, peer ^6||^7||^8). Vite 8 swaps Rollup+esbuild
for Rolldown with documented CJS-interop changes — and CJS main/preload emission is exactly what
the sandboxed-preload strategy above depends on. Matches apps/orb, which resolved to 7.3.6 too.
Versions pinned exactly, never caret ranges — same rule apps/orb applies.
